explanation: async marks method as asynchronous; await suspends execution until Task.Delay completes.
Using .Result blocks synchronously on async method, blocking the thread waiting for itself.
Task.Run executes delegate on thread pool; 5 + 3 = 8.
ConfigureAwait(false) prevents resuming on original context, improving performance.
WhenAll waits for all tasks to complete; time is max delay (100ms), not sum.
WhenAny completes when first task finishes; t1 (50ms) completes first.
CancellationToken allows cancellation; IsCancellationRequested becomes true after Cancel().
ValueTask is a lightweight alternative to Task; avoids allocation for synchronous completion.
Compiler transforms async method into state machine handling continuation at each await.
async void is fire-and-forget; caller can't await it or handle exceptions, should avoid.
